coaching.title: Easy 4mi Z2 + Strength
coaching.message: Week 1 re-entry off illness — this is a rebuild day, not a fitness day. 4 flat miles fully conversational, HR pinned 138-150. If it drifts high, walk it down; effort governs, not pace. Then Strength Session 1: single-leg work, hip stability, core, 2-3 sets. That hip and single-leg strength is exactly what holds your form together on Julian Alps' long alpine descents. Skip it if the body still feels flat from being sick.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Short easy session, so no mid-run fueling needed — just run topped-up, not stuffed. Coming off illness, prioritize hydration with electrolytes before and after. The real fueling window is post-strength: 25-30g protein plus carbs within 45 minutes to rebuild. Keep total intake solid today (aim near your ~220g carb baseline) — under-fueling a recovery week just stretches out getting your immune system fully back.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: You're an easy run and a light lift on a travel day (heading to San Salvador tomorrow) — the load is low, so make sleep the headline. Target 8+ hours tonight; immune recovery still trumps training this week. Ten minutes of hip and calf mobility after the strength work, hydrate on the move, and don't chase intensity to 'make up' for the down week.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: 51 days to Kranjska Gora. It's tempting in Peak Phase to slam back to volume, but a patient re-entry week off illness is what protects the peak block ahead — you can't peak from a hole. Trust the easy. Consistency across time zones is your edge; every controlled aerobic mile now is deposited against 2,500m of Julian Alps vert in September.
